// A name declared inside the subtest closure is not automatically the
// testing.TB the closure was handed. `parent := held.tb` is a local
// declaration holding the enclosing test's TB, and the qt.New built from it
// reports its failures against the parent test exactly as `qt.New(held.tb)`
// does. Nothing else in the file gives it away: the closure's own parameter is
// never touched, and the enclosing-scope walk sees only `held`, which is
// neither a checker nor a testing.TB.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

type fixtureTB struct {
	tb testing.TB
}

func newTB(tb testing.TB) testing.TB { return tb }

func TestCheckerFromALocalCopyOfAFieldTB(t *testing.T) {
	held := fixtureTB{tb: t}

	t.Run("the local name holds the parent's TB", func(t *testing.T) {
		parent := held.tb
		c := qt.New(parent)
		c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
	})
}

func TestCheckerFromALocalCopyTwoStepsOn(t *testing.T) {
	held := fixtureTB{tb: t}

	t.Run("the copy is one name further away", func(t *testing.T) {
		first := held.tb
		second := first
		c := qt.New(second)
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})
}

// The five local spellings that are the TB this closure was handed, and must
// stay silent: the parameter itself, a copy of it, a var with the type written
// out, a conversion of it, and the parameter of a helper closure written inside
// the subtest.
func TestConformingLocalTBSources(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("the closure's own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(t)
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	})

	t.Run("a copy of the closure's own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		own := t
		c := qt.New(own)
		c.Assert(4, qt.Equals, 4)
	})

	t.Run("a var whose type is written out", func(t *testing.T) {
		var own testing.TB = t
		c := qt.New(own)
		c.Assert(5, qt.Equals, 5)
	})

	t.Run("a conversion of the closure's own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		tb := testing.TB(t)
		c := qt.New(tb)
		c.Assert(6, qt.Equals, 6)
	})

	t.Run("a helper closure builds from the TB it was handed", func(t *testing.T) {
		nested := func(tb testing.TB) {
			inner := qt.New(tb)
			inner.Assert(7, qt.Equals, 7)
		}
		nested(t)
	})
}

// A conversion changes the static type of a value, never which test it belongs
// to, so seeing through it must not become a way out of the rule either.
func TestCheckerFromAConvertedFieldTB(t *testing.T) {
	held := fixtureTB{tb: t}

	t.Run("the conversion does not change whose TB it is", func(t *testing.T) {
		tb := testing.TB(held.tb)
		c := qt.New(tb)
		c.Assert(8, qt.Equals, 8)
	})
}

// A call is not a conversion. What newTB returns is decided by a body this
// package does not read, so the argument is reported rather than guessed at,
// and the message says which line to write instead. No call site in this
// repository builds a subtest checker this way.
func TestCheckerFromACallResult(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("a TB a call returned is not evidently the handed one", func(t *testing.T) {
		tb := newTB(t)
		c := qt.New(tb)
		c.Assert(9, qt.Equals, 9)
	})
}
